annotations.title: The wordes of the Gatherer.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Some Interpreters take these foure Hebrew wordes, Agur, Iache, Ithiel, and Ual, conteined in this first verse, to be proper names of men, supposing that a certaine wiseman named Agur, the sonne of Iache, spake the sentences folowing in this chapter, to his sonnes or schollars, called Ithiel & Ual. And so this supposed Agur, not Salomon, should be the auctor of this chapter. But the old Interpreter, whom S. Ierom approueth and foloweth, translated the same wordes as nounes appellatiues. Neither doth anie ancient Father account this Agur, amongst the writers of holie Scriptures. And if there were a peculiar auctor of this chapter, it is like the same should haue bene placed last, and not before that which now foloweth, and is by al men confessed to be Salomons. And therfore we thinke it more probable, with S. Beda, and the common opinion, that there was no other auctor of anie part of this booke, besides King Salomon. VVho is here called <sc>CONGREGANS</sc>, the Gatherer, <mn>[2]</mn> because he gathered these excellent Parables, and Prouerbes; as the sonne of the Holie Ghost, signified by the word <sc>IACHE</sc>, povvring forth diuine sentences, for instruction of <sc>ITHIEL</sc> & <sc>VCAL</sc>, that is, of al those vvith vvhom God is by his grace, and vvho are strengthened by God abiding vvith them.

notes.text: Some suppose one Agur to be author of this chapter. But it seemeth more probable that only Solomon is author of this whole book.

annotations.title: A bond woman when she shal be heyre.
annotations.text: Of al thinges in this world, it semeth most absurde, that heresie doth dominiere ouer Catholique religion: <mn>◦</mn> vvhich God some times, and in some places suffereth, for the greater merite of his elect.

notes.text: VVhy God suffereth heresie to reigne.
